fieldMarks: Stout body, total length 325-410 mm with tail 80-116 mm
Tawny nose and face; cinnamon-buff back over darker brown underfur
Eyes ringed with pale buff; legs and belly buffy; tail black
behavior: Colonial; about 70% of the year in hibernation
Active season about 86 days at higher elevations, about 100 at lower; emerges February-April
Active from about 20 minutes after sunrise
Eats roots, bulbs, stems, leaves, seeds, berries and some insects, mice or dead fish; may climb into shrubs and trees for buds and fruit
habitat: Alpine and subalpine meadows and other open habitat: high grass plateaus, sagebrush plains, valley grasslands, openings in conifer forest, stream banks.
range: Central Rocky Mountains from southeastern British Columbia and southwestern Alberta south through northern and eastern Washington, northeastern Oregon, northern and central Idaho and western Montana; mainly 700-8,000 ft.
